summary_en: This study tests defactinib and avutometinib given with nivolumab in patients with advanced lung adenocarcinoma that has an LKB1 mutation and did not respond to anti-PD1 treatment. Defactinib is taken by mouth twice a day on days 1 to 21, avutometinib is taken by mouth twice a week for 21 days, and nivolumab is given through a vein on day 1 of each 28-day cycle, repeated while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 2 study.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa defactinib y avutometinib administrados junto con nivolumab en pacientes con adenocarcinoma de pulmón avanzado que tiene una mutación de LKB1 y no respondió al tratamiento anti-PD1. El defactinib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día los días 1 al 21, el avutometinib se toma por vía oral dos veces por semana durante 21 días, y el nivolumab se administra por vena el día 1 de cada ciclo de 28 días, que se repite mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Advanced lung adenocarcinoma that is not suitable for surgery or combined modality treatment.
Known LKB1 mutation confirmed in the tumor.
Disease that progressed after immune checkpoint inhibitor and first-line chemotherapy.
Measurable disease, age 18 or older, and ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Adequate blood counts, liver function, kidney function, and recovery from prior treatment side effects.
not_for: Known treatable driver mutation with an FDA-approved targeted therapy, such as EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 (KRAS excepted).
Unstable or symptomatic brain metastasis, or known leptomeningeal disease.
Pre-existing autoimmune condition with higher risk from nivolumab, or serious autoimmune toxicity with prior checkpoint inhibitor.
Active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection that is active or needs therapy.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, current warfarin use, or history of rhabdomyolysis.
